consumer_seed: The Ofcom mobile-faults guide was published on 4 May 2017.
The Ofcom mobile-faults guide was last updated on 8 April 2026.
Building work that increases the number or thickness of walls can affect mobile-signal strength.
Ofcom advises recording where, when and what happened when a mobile fault occurs.
Ofcom advises checking expected coverage at a location using its mobile coverage checker.
Before moving home, customers can ask the provider or use the coverage checker to assess service at the new address.
If service at a new address is unsuitable, Ofcom advises asking what cancellation charge would apply.
A provider may ask a customer to clean and replace the SIM or test it in another unlocked device.
Most providers offer an online or app-based service-status checker for known large network issues.
The customer's provider is responsible for ensuring faults are fixed and for providing progress updates.
The provider remains responsible even when it uses another company's network.
For a network-service fault, the provider should explain how and when it will be fixed.
Fault updates may be provided through customer service, an app or registered fault alerts.
After allowing reasonable repair time, a customer can escalate concerns about a delayed repair.
Customers can ask whether calls or texts can be used over Wi-Fi while repairs are under way.
Depending on the circumstances, a provider may offer money back while repairs are made.
Long repairs may justify an additional refund or account credit in some cases.
A prolonged loss of service may give a customer a contractual right to leave without penalty, depending on the contract and facts.
If a fault is not repaired by the promised date, the customer can follow the provider's formal complaints procedure.
An unresolved mobile-fault complaint can go to ADR after six weeks, or earlier with a deadlock letter.
The Ofcom mobile-switching guide was published on 3 April 2023.
The mobile-switching process depends on whether the customer wants to keep the existing number.
Keeping a mobile number is called porting and requires a Porting Authorisation Code (PAC).
The Auto-Switch process can be used for one number or for multiple numbers up to 24.
A customer switching one number can request a PAC by texting PAC to 65075.
A PAC requested by phone must be given immediately or sent by text within two hours when immediate provision is not possible.
A PAC requested by text or online must be provided within two working days.
For two to 24 numbers, the PAC must be requested online or by phone.
For more than 24 numbers switched simultaneously, the customer must contact the current provider for instructions.
A PAC is valid for 30 days and a new PAC can be requested after expiry.
The current provider must send early-termination-charge information alongside the PAC.
After the new provider receives the PAC, the number should normally be ported within one working day.
A customer not keeping the number should request a Service Termination Authorisation Code (STAC).
A customer switching one number without keeping it can text STAC to 75075.
For two to 24 numbers, a STAC can be requested by phone or through the online account.
Mobile providers cannot charge for notice periods running after the switch date.
Providing the PAC or STAC lets the old and new providers coordinate to avoid double payment.
A switch taking more than one working day, or abuse of the process, can entitle the customer to reasonable compensation.
Providers must explain how delayed-switch compensation can be accessed and paid.
A customer can ask the new provider to keep a cancelled number for free when the request is made within one month of cancellation.
The Ofcom checker-update page was published on 26 May 2021.
The Ofcom checker-update page was last updated on 28 June 2023.
The checker changes were intended to improve accessibility and show which companies offer services in an area.
The checker can show indoor and outdoor mobile availability for calls and mobile internet from major providers.
The checker can display broadband availability for a UK address.
The checker provides tips for improving internet connection or mobile coverage.
The checker requires a postcode and address to return its detailed results.
Broadband results can include standard, superfast and ultrafast service availability.
Mobile checker data is based on signal-level predictions supplied by the four UK mobile network operators.
Broadband checker data is based on availability and predicted-speed data supplied by major UK internet service providers.
Actual experience can differ from checker predictions because network use and other factors affect signals and speeds.
The coverage checker does not identify temporary local service problems; providers should supply that information.
The Ofcom telecoms-complaints report was published on 25 January 2024.
The Ofcom telecoms-complaints report was last updated on 30 July 2026.
Ofcom receives complaints about landline, fixed broadband, pay-monthly mobile and pay-TV services.
Ofcom compares providers quarterly using complaints received per 100,000 customers.
Overall Q1 2026 complaints decreased compared with Q4 2025.
Fixed-broadband and pay-monthly-mobile complaints decreased in Q1 2026.
Landline and pay-TV complaint levels stayed the same in Q1 2026.
Overall complaints returned to all-time-low levels in Q1 2026.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about fixed-broadband provider in Q1 2026.
Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed-broadband complaints in Q1 2026.
Plusnet and TalkTalk generated the most landline complaints in Q1 2026.
EE, Sky, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Vodafone were the least complained-about landline providers in Q1 2026.
Sky Mobile was the most complained-about pay-monthly-mobile provider in Q1 2026.
Sky Mobile complaints were primarily driven by customer experiences when changing provider.
EE, Giffgaff, Tesco Mobile, Three and Vodafone generated the fewest pay-monthly-mobile complaints in Q1 2026.
EE and Virgin Media were the most complained-about pay-TV providers in Q1 2026.
EE pay-TV complaints were mainly about complaint handling.
Virgin Media pay-TV complaints were mainly about billing, pricing and charges.
Sky and TalkTalk generated the fewest pay-TV complaints in Q1 2026.
Year on year, the relative volume of fixed-broadband complaints decreased.
Year on year, the relative volume of landline complaints decreased.
Year on year, the relative volume of pay-monthly-mobile complaints increased.
Year on year, the relative volume of pay-TV complaints stayed the same.
Ofcom directs users to its background and methodology document for provider-comparability details.
expansion_rule: For each July 2026 BDUK contract emit twelve records: supplier, contracted, built, built share, contracted-total share, built-total share, unbuilt gap, unbuilt share, contracted rank, built rank, completion rank and percentage-point difference from displayed overall completion. Append 76 Ofcom mobile-fault, mobile-switching, checker and complaints records. Equal numeric values share competition rank. Every fifth expanded record is REVALIDATION; all others are UPGRADE.
